## Before submitting

- [ ] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes (none required).
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches; see the testing-policy exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: `cat-perf-bug`, `area:sparse_attention`, and `orig-nv-eng`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: SM100/SM103 BF16 block sparse attention.

## Summary

Long fixed-count KV rows previously stayed unsplit whenever the Q grid had at least 512 tiles. Auto selection now permits four splits for 450–899 active KV blocks and eight splits for 900 or more, including large-Q workloads. Large-Q variable-count rows and shorter fixed-count rows retain one split; short-Q selection and workspace-budget fallback remain in place.

The blk64 forward and combine paths write directly into the requested BHSD/BSHD output layout, eliminating output transpose copies and avoiding forced BHSD copies of contiguous BSHD inputs. The SM100 blk64 backward kernel derives O, dO, and dQ views from each tensor's own layout rather than reusing Q's layout. Documentation and the existing auto-selection test are updated.

## Why

Long fixed-count rows can benefit from split-KV even when there are enough independent Q tiles to fill the GPU. Variable-row index capacity can substantially overestimate real work, so large-Q variable-count workloads remain conservative. Native layout handling removes copies that would otherwise add overhead to these paths.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

No public signature or dependency changes. BF16 auto split selection changes for long fixed-count rows. Explicit splits, workspace-budget fallback, contiguous output contracts, and the separate Sage FP8 policy are preserved. The new private combine argument is appended with a default.

## Testing

On NVIDIA B200 (SM100), cuDNN 9.22.0, PyTorch 2.12.0a0, CUDA 13.2:

- BSA forward/backward L0 suites: **22 passed, 23 skipped** (31.42 seconds). Ran `pytest.main(["-n", "0", "-q", "block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_attention_forward.py", "block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_attention_backward.py"])` from `test/python` using a source-package launcher. The launcher loaded this checkout's `python/cudnn/__init__.py` with the installed compiled extension available as a secondary package search path; both the conftest banner and BSA interface path confirmed this checkout was under test.
- `python -m pre_commit run --files docs/fe-oss-apis/bsa.md python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/_interface.py python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/csrc/bwd/sm100_blk64/bsa_bwd_sm100.py test/python/block_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_BSA_attention_forward.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/develop...HEAD`: passed.

Testing-policy exception: the existing `test_bsa_attention_forward_sm100_blk64_large_q_auto_scheduler_policy` continues to assert exact heuristic choices, updated for this tuning change. These assertions describe the current policy, not a semantic requirement; future tuning may update them (see `test/AGENTS.md`, “Heuristic tests must survive legitimate tuning changes”).

No new performance benchmark was run during PR preparation; these checks establish correctness, not measured speedup.

+automatic scheduler policy has not been tuned for that combination.
+
+The BF16 automatic policy is tuned assuming approximately uniform random KV
+indices with little overlap between the neighborhoods of different Q blocks.
+It uses host-visible tensor metadata and device properties, without reading
+indices or counts back to the host. Highly overlapping, shared or local-window
+indices can favor a different split count even at the same shape and density;
+benchmark explicit `kv_splits` values for those masks. This assumption affects
+performance only, not attention semantics or supported mask patterns.
+
+For fewer than 512 total Q tiles (`B * H * ceil(S_q / 64)`), the existing policy
+uses the fixed active block count, or index capacity for variable counts:
+256--449 blocks select two splits, 450--899 select four, and 900 or more select
+eight. Larger Q grids keep one split except in the measured long-Q region:
+BF16 MHA with Q/K/V head dimensions 128, `S_q >= 262144`, a fixed count of at
+least 512 active KV blocks, and density at most 1/8 (active blocks divided by
+`ceil(S_k / 64)`). In that region, K+V bytes **per batch and KV head** above twice
+the device L2 size select eight splits for at least 900 active blocks and four
+or more heads; a single head requires at least 1024 active blocks. Otherwise,
+four or more heads select four splits when per-head K+V bytes exceed L2.
+All other cases, including an unavailable L2 size, keep one split. Variable
+per-row counts also keep one split on larger Q grids because index capacity
+does not describe actual row work. The Sage FP8 policy is separate.
+
+Automatic selection
 falls back to a smaller split count when the estimated live workspace does not
 fit the available CUDA allocator budget; an explicit split count that exceeds
 that budget raises `RuntimeError`.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `7dab9567ed86` against base `33c6fcb54d11`.

The native layout changes are useful: mixed-layout backward cases fail on develop and pass with this change, and avoiding BSHD copies improves the measured unsplit forward path. I am withholding approval for the broader automatic split policy, which reproducibly regresses a supported long-Q workload. Please retain the layout fixes and narrow or defer the heuristic change until its winning region is measured. This affects callers selecting kv_splits='auto'; the explicit/default kv_splits=1 route is unchanged. Labels, project and milestone are already appropriate.

**[P1 · blocks approval] Bound the new large-Q split policy by measured benefit** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/7dab9567ed860bc9348b881640bfbb1bdba48362/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/_interface.py#L417))

The 900-block rule now selects eight splits regardless of how much Q parallelism is already available. For BF16 B=1, H=8, Sq=16384, Sk=57600, D=128, fixed indices 0..899 in every row, and kv_splits='auto', an interleaved develop/integrated-head/head/develop comparison on one SM100 device gives BHSD GPU replay 4.654 -> 5.526 ms (+18.7%) and host calls 46.4 -> 341.2 us. BSHD also regresses 5.160 -> 5.528 ms (+7.1%), despite removing its copies. A same-code 1/auto/auto/1 control on a second SM100 device confirms the policy effect: BHSD 10.489 -> 12.325 ms (+17.5%), BSHD 10.483 -> 12.330 ms (+17.6%); their host calls rise about 5.3x and 5.9x. Please preserve the previous large-Q policy until a workload/device-aware boundary is supported by measurements, or restrict the new rule to its demonstrated winning region. This is high P1 because a supported automatic choice repeatedly loses substantial GPU time and host throughput in the exact long-Q class being broadened; I would address it before merging. These are SM100 spot checks, not GB200 qualification or serving-throughput claims.

Evidence: Public CuTeDSL4.8.0 and Torch2.14.1, exact source binding. First comparison used current develop33c6fcb and its isolated merge with7dab956. Eight shapes/layouts measured in base/head/head/base order; analytic O/LSE checks before timing and changed-input graph replay checks after timing all passed. A second SM100 used the same integrated source and 1/auto/auto/1 policy order. The neutral 449-block BHSD control stayed flat (691.05 -> 691.12 us), while its BSHD counterpart improved 923.92 -> 691.45 us. Q/K were zero and V varied by head, making the correctness oracle exact without a large dense reference. Attribution: Introduced by expanding automatic splitting to previously unsplit large-Q fixed-count rows; the independent native-layout optimization is beneficial.

**[P2] Add the mixed-layout regression that motivates the backward fix** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/7dab9567ed860bc9348b881640bfbb1bdba48362/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention/csrc/bwd/sm100_blk64/bsa_bwd_sm100.py#L255))

The per-tensor layout fix works, but the PR's only test change asserts a new heuristic winner. Please retain a numerical regression with Q, O, dO and caller-provided dQ in different physical layouts, under both BHSD and BSHD declarations. My B=2/H=3/Sq=128/Sk=320/D=128 test, with query-dependent three-block selections, fails all four mixed-layout backward combinations on develop and passes all four with this change, including all three gradients and output-buffer identity. Cover both unsplit and split forward output feeding backward. This would protect the actual correctness fix; the exact 4/8-split choices belong in the offline performance evidence rather than a correctness golden, as test/AGENTS.md explains.

Evidence: Independent source-pinned probe: 12 forward cases, four backward combinations checking 12 gradients, and four changed-input CUDA-graph replays pass in the integrated tree. The same full-tile probe is RED on develop for the mixed-layout gradients while forward/replay controls remain green. Attribution: Missing regression coverage for the correctness change in this PR; independently verified fix.

Validation: Original head on native SM100: existing BSA forward/backward L0 suites, 22 passed and 23 skipped. Isolated merge with current develop auto-merges cleanly; its expanded suites give 34 passed, 33 skipped and 60 deselected. Integrated mixed-layout probe: 12 forward cases at splits1/2/4, four backward combinations with caller-provided gradient buffers, and four changed-input CUDA-graph replays passed. Develop fails the corresponding mixed-layout backward controls, demonstrating that this fix matters. Interleaved performance controls separately measured CPU call submission and CUDA-event graph replay; all analytic output and LSE checks passed, including changed V values after capture. The native BSHD unsplit control improves, while the newly selected large-Q split route regresses as detailed above. A separate Sq=129 all-contiguous backward probe exposes an existing partial-Q problem: develop and the integrated head have identical failure counts and maximum absolute errors (dQ0.2596, dK0.1641, dV0.5201); their forward and replay controls pass. This deserves a separate follow-up and is not attributed to the layout change.

Limitations: Local SM100 evidence does not establish GB200/B200/SM103 performance. Please attach the target-workload measurements motivating the 450/900 thresholds; the current PR description explicitly has no performance results. The native extension was reused only for import/runtime support; this review exercises the Python/CuTe BSA route. It does not qualify unrelated native API changes between the old PR base and current develop. No CI was triggered because the automatic-policy regression needs resolution first. Existing style and documentation checks passed.

I am withholding approval for the high-risk P1 findings above and leaving a COMMENT. Please address them before merging.
